difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:ccs-properties at source lines 504-528: a complete Sigma-consistent set Gamma is deductively closed, contains Sigma, contains the truth constant but not the falsity constant, and its membership relation mirrors each propositional connective, that is, negation, conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional. The proof at source lines 530-597 is a long case-by-case verification with a uniform but non-trivial pattern. Each clause has to be derived from the two defining properties of Gamma, completeness and Sigma-consistency, together with the fact that certain schemas are tautological instances and hence provable in Sigma: for instance the conjunction case runs the argument in both directions using the tautologies (A and B) implies A, and A implies (B implies (A and B)), the disjunction case argues through the negations of both disjuncts, the implication case uses the tautologies that extract the antecedent and the negation of the consequent from the negation of the implication, and the biconditional case combines the two directions. The earlier clauses are then reused inside the later ones, and the ordering of the cases matters. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
